name: SpaceX
day_summary: BOND DISTRIBUTION GRINDS LOWER — STEP ASIDE UNCHANGED. SPCX closed June 24 at $154.54 (-$1.57, -1.01% from $156.11 prev close), session range $150.72–$159.86. The bond distribution supply overhang from the $20B SpaceX inaugural offering (June 22, $89B demand, 4.4x oversubscribed) continues to mechanically weigh on equity as institutional bond allocants rebalance cross-asset exposures. The $150.72 intraday low approached but did not breach the $150 IG ratings defense line on a closing basis ($154.54 close is $4.54 above the $150 floor). The NVDA Annual Meeting + Micron Q3 risk-on session provided a temporary bid: SPCX recovered from session lows toward $159.86 intraday before settling at $154.54. Step-aside posture UNCHANGED at HIGH conviction. Re-entry requires two consecutive daily closes above $185 on above-average volume — currently $30.46 away (+19.7%). Bond distribution clears approximately July 1–6. September 2 first earnings remains the structural re-entry catalyst.

decision.rationale: STEP ASIDE at HIGH conviction — UNCHANGED. The June 24 session confirmed the bond distribution supply dynamic: SPCX closed at $154.54 (-1.01%), grinding lower despite the NVDA Annual Meeting + Micron Q3 risk-on macro environment. The two-consecutive-close gate ($185, above-average volume) is the only quantitative re-entry signal — and at $154.54, SPCX is $30.46 away (+19.7%) from Day 1 of the gate.
